prompt: Which file is the page at `/about`?

choices.text: `src/routes/(about)/+page.svelte`
choices.why: Brackets make a group, which adds nothing to the address: that file would be `/`.

choices.text: `src/routes/about.svelte`
choices.why: A page is the `+page.svelte` inside a folder, not a file named after the address.

choices.text: `src/routes/about/+page.svelte`
choices.why: Right: the folder `about` gives the address, and `+page.svelte` is the page in it.

choices.text: `src/lib/about/+page.svelte`
choices.why: `src/lib` is for code the pages use; the router reads only `src/routes`.

prompt: You save `Chart.svelte` next to `+page.svelte` in `src/routes/stats/`. What does the router do with it?

choices.text: Nothing; it is ignored
choices.why: Right. Only names starting with `+` are the router's; the page can still import it.

choices.text: Refuses to start, because a route folder may hold only `+` files
choices.why: A helper may sit next to the page that uses it.

choices.text: Wraps the page in it, like a layout
choices.why: That is `+layout.svelte`'s job, and it needs the name.

choices.text: Serves it as a second page, at `/stats/Chart`
choices.why: Only `+page.svelte` makes a page.

prompt: You click "Back to the planner" on `/about`. What does SvelteKit do?
hint: `look` printed `at /`, and the section explains how it got there.

choices.text: Nothing, unless the link uses a special `<Link>` component
choices.why: There is no link component; a plain `<a href>` is enough.

choices.text: Renders the new page in place and updates the address with the History API
choices.why: Right: a client-side navigation, with no reload.

choices.text: Lets the browser load `/` from the server and draw it from scratch, as any link on any site would
choices.why: That would be a reload, which SvelteKit avoids for its own pages.

prompt: To set a page's title, put a `<title>` inside `<svelte:___>`.
Where does a page go inside a `+layout.svelte`?
hint: The layout receives it as a prop.

choices.text: After the layout's own markup, always
choices.why: The layout chooses the spot; here it is inside `<main>`.

choices.text: Inside the first `<main>` it finds
choices.why: Nothing looks for a `<main>`; the layout says where.

choices.text: Wherever the layout puts a `<slot />`
choices.why: Svelte 5 renders a snippet; slots are the old way.

choices.text: Where it writes `{@render children()}`
choices.why: Right: `children` is the page, as a snippet.

prompt: You move from `/` to `/about`. What happens to the root layout?

choices.text: It stays, and only the `children` it renders changes
choices.why: Right: a layout is not recreated between two pages it wraps.

choices.text: It is destroyed and created again for the new page
choices.why: That would lose its state on every click, which is what layouts avoid.

choices.text: It is rendered again on the server and sent whole
choices.why: A client-side navigation does not ask the server for the layout again.

prompt: What is the address of `src/routes/(planner)/+page.svelte`?

prompt: Why does About go in a group of its own, `(info)`?
hint: What does the `(planner)` layout do before it renders a page?

choices.text: So it does not wait for the planner's data, which it never uses
choices.why: Right: only the planner's pages need the data and the context.

choices.text: To give it the address `/info/about`
choices.why: A group adds nothing to the address; About is still `/about`.

choices.text: So the header is not drawn above it
choices.why: The header is the root layout's, which wraps both groups.

choices.text: Because SvelteKit requires every page to be in some group
choices.why: Pages outside any group are fine; the root layout wraps them.

prompt: The week page sets its title with `<svelte:head>` instead of an effect. What does that gain?

choices.text: The title is in the HTML the server sends
choices.why: Right: effects run only in the browser, `<svelte:head>` also on the server.

choices.text: It removes the need for a root layout
choices.why: The layout is still there; the title is a separate matter.

choices.text: The title updates faster when the total changes
choices.why: Speed is not the point; both follow the total.
